items.name: SUB · Get price
items.what: Sub-workflow behind get_price: matches one product by aliases in Price_List and returns a small found / not-found-with-suggestions / error result.
setup: Make sure your sheet has a Price_List tab with columns sku, name, unit, price, stock, aliases, active (the Boss 3 sheet).
Create (or reuse) a Google Sheets OAuth2 credential and select it in Price_List.
Replace YOUR_SHEET_ID in Price_List with your sheet's ID.
Save the workflow and note its ID.
items.test: Pin test data on the trigger such as {"product": "big tatashe"} and execute: you should get found: true, Tatashe pepper, 9000. Then try "pepper" (found: false with Tatashe pepper and Rodo as suggestions) and "yam" (found: false).

items.name: HL · Quote agent (4.2)
items.what: The 4.1 agent with get_price and a calculator added, plus the lesson's price, arithmetic and delivery rules in the system message.
setup: Import SUB · Get price and SUB · Get FAQ (4.1) first and save them.
Create an OpenAI credential and select it in Chat model. Replace YOUR_MODEL with the model you use.
In get_price, replace YOUR_GET_PRICE_WORKFLOW_ID by choosing SUB · Get price from the list.
In get_faq, replace YOUR_GET_FAQ_WORKFLOW_ID by choosing SUB · Get FAQ from the list.
Open Settings → Error workflow and choose HL · Error alerts.
items.test: In the chat, ask "How much for 3 crates of tomatoes and 2 bags of tatashe delivered to Bodija?": the log should show two get_price calls and one calculator call, and the answer should be ₦55,500 with free delivery. Then ask "2 baskets of pepper": it should ask whether you mean rodo or tatashe.

walk.title: Build it: exact quotes, every time
walk.sample: Chat: How much for 3 crates of tomatoes and 2 bags of tatashe delivered to Bodija?

steps.say: We take the 4.1 FAQ agent and give it two new tools: one to look up prices, one to do the sums. SUB Get price is already built and tested on its own.
show: Import SUB · Get price and SUB · Get FAQ first

steps.say: Same chat trigger as before, so you can test quotes right inside the editor.
show: Response Mode: When Last Node Finishes

steps.say: The agent keeps all the 4.1 rules. We add new ones: call get_price for every product before giving any number, and always use the calculator for totals.
show: Prices: always call get_price for every product
Arithmetic: always use the calculator for totals

steps.say: The delivery rule is written out once: one thousand five hundred naira, free from thirty thousand. And if a product isn't found, the agent must ask which one they mean.
show: If get_price returns found: false, ask, using suggestions

steps.say: The brain is unchanged. It reads every tool's name and description on each call and picks what to do next.
get_faq stays, for hours, delivery days and payment questions. It still reads the FAQ sheet and nothing else.
Now the price tool, a Call n8n Workflow tool pointing at SUB Get price. Your tested matching code does the lookup, so the agent can't invent a price even if it tries.
The description says what it does, when to use it, what comes back, and what it's not for. That's the note the model chooses from.
show: Use this … before giving any number.
Returns found, name, unit, price in naira and stock.
Don't use it for delivery fees.

steps.say: One input, product, described with examples. One product per call keeps each result small and clear.
show: one product per call, e.g. tatashe, ugu, ata rodo

steps.say: Models are bad at sums, so money goes to the calculator. This template uses a small code tool that only accepts numbers and plus, minus, times, divide.
If anything breaks, the error output still replies to the customer, and the error workflow tells Tolu.
show: Settings → Error workflow: HL · Error alerts

steps.say: Ask the Bodija question and read the trace. You want two get_price calls, one calculator call, and fifty five thousand five hundred naira with free delivery.
Then try two baskets of pepper. Pepper is ambiguous, so the tool returns suggestions and the agent asks: rodo or tatashe?

walk.end: Two lookups, one sum, zero naira difference from the price list: that's a quote you can trust.
